newsitem.title: UK: DIARY - Today in Westminster - Nov 13.
newsitem.headline: DIARY - Today in Westminster - Nov 13.

text.p: The House of Commons will discuss the "mad cow" crisis and the export ban on British beef in a debate expected to begin around 1530 GMT on Wednesday.
The debate will be on a motion from the opposition Labour Party criticising the government's handling of the issue.
Other events scheduled at Westminster include -
- Education and Employment questions at 1430 GMT.
- Transport Committee questions Transport Department on government plans to privatise National Air Traffic Services, 1600 GMT.
- Home Affairs Committee questions Chief Inspector of Prisons Sir John Learmont on the prison service, 1645 GMT.

- James Arbuthnot, minister of defence procurement, gives evidence to Defence Committee on sale of married quarters estate. Other witnesses are the buyer of the estate, Annington Homes, and the Defence Housing Executive. 1030 BST/GMT
- Foreign Affairs Committee holds inquiry into development of UK links and business in Latin America. Witnesses include FCO minister Sir Nicholas Bonsor. 1030 GMT.
- National Heritage Committee, inquiring into proposed curbs on chequebook journalism, hears from Lord Chancellor Lord Mackay. 1600 GMT
- Trade and Industry Committee hears evidence from former Energy Minister Tim Eggar on Energy Regulation, 1030 GMT. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
